title: Show HN: I trained a 125M model to autocomplete piano on-device
content:
The thread discusses a user-developed **125M-parameter transformer model** designed to perform real-time, on-device piano autocomplete on an iPhone. Users can play MIDI notes, and the model continues the musical phrase, functioning similarly to code-completion tools like GitHub Copilot.

### Key Technical Details:
*   **Performance:** The model runs at roughly 108 notes/second on an iPhone 15, achieved by optimizing note representations (reducing autoregressive passes) and using Core ML.
*   **Data:** The model was pretrained on roughly 300 million note events from hundreds of thousands of MIDI files and fine-tuned using DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) with a small set of preference examples.
*   **Infrastructure:** The creator trained the model using 4x RTX 4090s, avoiding cloud GPU costs.

### Community Reaction & Discussion:
*   **Musical Context:** Participants shared historical insights, noting that "autocomplete" mimics traditional classical improvisation and "audiation" practices used by composers like Rachmaninoff. There was debate regarding the aesthetic quality of the model’s output, with some pointing out that it lacks the structural complexity and phrasing idiomatic to the Classical/Romantic eras.
*   **Creative Philosophy:** A significant portion of the discussion centered on the role of AI in art. While some critics argued that such tools diminish the value of learning traditional music theory and practice, others defended the project as a "fun, quaint" technical experiment or a useful tool for rapid ideation and experimentation.
*   **Feature Requests & Future Directions:**
    *   **Expandability:** Suggestions included adding support for MIDI velocity, pedal data, and complex instrumentation (backing tracks/orchestration).
    *   **Integration:** Users expressed interest in VST/Max 4 Live support, Web MIDI, or feeding the output back into physical player pianos.
    *   **Improvements:** Suggestions included adding "Chain of Thought" (CoT) reasoning for better long-term compositional planning and comparing the model's output to other projects like Google’s *Magenta*.

The thread reflects the broader HN divide between enthusiasm for technical "tinkering" and concerns over the societal and creative implications of generative AI.

title: Show HN: Huzzah – a novel approach to coding with AI
content:
The discussion centers on the release of **Huzzah**, an experimental code editor designed to address the fatigue caused by constant LLM-based prompting. The author introduces a paradigm where developers write **pseudocode** that is persisted alongside the generated source code, serving as a permanent, human-readable record of intent.

### Key Arguments and Perspectives

*   **The Problem with "Vibe Coding":** Many users agree with the author that current agent-based development is exhausting. Critics argue that delegating all thinking to an AI turns programming from a "meditative" or creative process into a draining, managerial task of "barking orders" at an agent.
*   **The "Intent Gap":** A recurring theme is the loss of "human intent" in modern AI-assisted workflows. Prompts are ephemeral and discarded, leaving developers with AI-generated code that is often difficult to understand, debug, or maintain. Huzzah’s core value proposition—persisting the intent as a pseudocode "source of truth"—was generally praised as a solution to this.
*   **Skepticism and Counter-Proposals:**
    *   **Is it a New Language?** Some critics argued that Huzzah effectively reinventing a custom DSL or transpiler, which introduces new overhead and cognitive load.
    *   **Existing Alternatives:** Numerous users pointed out that similar goals can be achieved via existing methods, such as:
        *   **Behavior-Driven Development (BDD):** Using Gherkin/Cucumber syntax to define requirements and executable tests.
        *   **Architectural Decision Records (ADRs):** Keeping a "ledger" of why changes were made.
        *   **Custom Tooling:** Some developers shared their own CLI-based harnesses, Git-based workflows (logging prompts in Git notes), or IDE-native approaches to maintain accountability.
*   **Philosophical Divide:** 
    *   **The "New World" Perspective:** Some participants argue that software engineering has fundamentally changed and that resistance to AI-driven workflows is a futile struggle for an obsolete skill set. 
    *   **The "Human-in-the-Loop" Perspective:** Others argue that complex, large-scale systems will always require a human to define the "what" and "why." They view the current "agent-everywhere" trend as a temporary peak that will eventually balance out once the industry realizes that auditability and human-verifiable intent are non-negotiable for serious software.

### Consensus on the Project
While many were skeptical about the specific implementation—specifically the need for a separate editor UI rather than an IDE plugin—the community found the core concept (persisting human-written intent as a first-class citizen in the codebase) highly relevant. Several participants expressed interest in seeing the project evolve to handle multi-file systems, source-mapping between the pseudocode and real code, and more robust error handling for AI-generated output.

title: Show HN: Open-source Stripe Connect alternative
content:
The thread introduces **Zoneless**, an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Stripe Connect designed for global marketplace payouts. The creator, Ben, explains that the platform utilizes stablecoins (USDC) to drastically reduce payout fees and bypass the geographic limitations of traditional payment processors.

### **Key Discussion Points:**

*   **Value Proposition:** Ben built Zoneless after finding Stripe Connect fees unsustainable for his own marketplace, PromptBase. He notes that 74% of his sellers prefer the Zoneless payout option over traditional methods.
*   **Compliance and Risk:** A former Stripe Connect engineer raised concerns about money laundering, fraud, and the lack of robust identity verification. Ben responded that Zoneless integrates with **Didit** for KYC, checks against OFAC sanctions lists, and monitors for suspicious activity.
*   **Technical Implementation:**
    *   **Self-Hosting vs. Managed:** Users can either self-host for minimal network fees (~$0.002 per transaction) or use the managed version.
    *   **Independent Rails:** The system is independent of Stripe; users can use a traditional processor for checkout/collections while using Zoneless specifically for global payouts to avoid high fees.
    *   **Stablecoins:** Discussion centered on the stability of USDC compared to other cryptocurrencies, with users debating the regulatory, banking, and systematic risks of relying on stablecoins.
*   **Community Reception:**
    *   **Positive:** Many users praised the aesthetics and design of the project, as well as the utility of having an open-source option for niche marketplaces.
    *   **Critical/Constructive:** Some commenters pointed out the friction involved in converting and holding USDC, as well as the ongoing need for rigorous compliance. There was also a spirited defense of the project against "gatekeeping" or overly aggressive criticism regarding its current KYC/AML status.
    *   **Comparisons:** The thread compared Zoneless to similar platforms like Coinflow and Usedots, with the creator emphasizing that the open-source, fee-free nature of Zoneless is its primary differentiator.

title: Show HN: Check if any of the $656M in unclaimed royalties at The MLC is yours
content:
The thread discusses the launch of a tool (pub.doub.ly) designed to help musicians identify and claim unpaid "mechanical royalties" held by The MLC (The Mechanical Licensing Collective). 

**Key takeaways from the discussion:**

*   **The Problem:** Under the 2018 Music Modernization Act (MMA), The MLC collects mechanical royalties for digital streams. Millions of dollars remain unclaimed ("the black box") due to poor metadata or registration issues. Starting in January 2027, unclaimed funds will be distributed via a "market share" pro-rata process that largely benefits major publishers over independent artists.
*   **The Tool:** The creator built a free, self-service utility where artists can enter a Spotify link to check if their songs are correctly registered with The MLC. It flags missing or unmatched metadata and provides direct links to the MLC tools needed to fix these issues.
*   **Technical & Industry Nuance:**
    *   **Data Estimation:** The tool estimates potential earnings based on Spotify stream counts, which some users noted can lead to inaccuracies. The creator clarified that the estimates combine actual MLC data "brackets" with Spotify stream modeling to provide a projected range.
    *   **System Load:** The tool experienced significant traffic ("the HN hug"), leading to temporary rate-limiting issues with the Spotify API, which the developer actively managed throughout the day.
    *   **Educational Gap:** Several users pointed out that the industry jargon (like "MLC" and "mechanical royalties") is opaque; the creator acknowledged the need to add more context to the site for non-industry professionals.
*   **Reception:** The community generally praised the utility of the project as a vital resource for independent artists to recover lost income, even while noting the complexities and assumptions involved in calculating the "at-risk" funds. The developer maintained full transparency regarding their commercial interest in the space while emphasizing that the tool itself is free and requires no signup.

title: Show HN: We chased a weather balloon across Montana and never found it
content:
This thread discusses the "UpLink" project, a high-altitude weather balloon experiment conducted by two high school students. The project involved designing custom electronics, firmware, and a 3D-printed payload to capture and transmit images from the stratosphere.

**Key points from the discussion include:**

*   **Engineering & Design:** The authors explain their choice of 3D printing for the payload housing, citing the need for precise mounting for cameras and antennas, as well as the convenience of iterating designs during prototyping. Other users suggest that foam (Styrofoam) could have been a cheaper, more customizable alternative.
*   **Technical Challenges:**
    *   **Data Transmission:** The team used LoRa on the 915 MHz band to transmit images. Commenters suggested alternative protocols like SSTV or lower-frequency ham bands for better efficiency, though the authors noted battery power constraints influenced their current design.
    *   **Atmospheric Data:** Discussion arose regarding unexpected temperature readings at high altitudes, with the author clarifying that solar heating likely skewed their ground-level sensor data.
*   **Community Feedback:**
    *   Many commenters praised the students for their high level of technical competency at a young age.
    *   A local resident from Montana offered to look for the lost payload, noting the harsh wind conditions in the area.
    *   Other topics included the safety considerations of using hydrogen vs. helium and interest in potential ballooning hobbyist groups.

The project source code and documentation are available on GitHub, and the received images can be viewed in an online gallery provided by the developers.

title: Show HN: Omacosy – Omarchy-style tiling desktop for macOS, no SIP
content:
The thread discusses the launch of **Omacosy**, a macOS project designed to recreate an "Omarchy-style" tiling desktop experience. The creator built this using **AeroSpace** (to maintain System Integrity Protection/SIP), Karabiner, and custom Swift binaries, aiming to provide a keyboard-driven workflow similar to Hyprland.

### Key discussion points include:

*   **The Struggle with macOS UI:** Many users expressed frustration with macOS for professional tasks, citing inconsistent dock behavior, broken window management, and poor support for tiling. Several contributors noted that trying to force a tiling workflow onto macOS often leads to minor, daily "hacks" that can be unstable.
*   **AeroSpace vs. Yabai:** The creator opted for AeroSpace specifically to avoid disabling SIP, a security feature that Yabai often requires for advanced functionality.
*   **Instant Space Switching:** A significant sub-discussion emerged regarding the animation lag when switching macOS desktops. Users shared tools like **InstantSpaceSwitcher** and **Space Rabbit** as effective solutions to achieve "instant" switching.
*   **Community Feedback & Advice:**
    *   **Transparency/Trust:** Some users advised the creator to remove AI-generated language ("Claude-ese") from their documentation to build better community trust.
    *   **Project Maturity:** The creator clarified that a reference to "Korren" in the code was an unintended "sneak peek" at a terminal emulator they are currently developing.
    *   **Sustainability:** Users questioned why such quality workflow-enhancing tools aren't funded by accelerators like YC, with the consensus being that these projects are typically driven by passion rather than commercial intent.

Overall, the project was well-received by developers looking for a more "Linux-like" tiling experience on their MacBooks, though the conversation served as a sounding board for the inherent difficulties of customizing a highly opinionated and restricted operating system like macOS.

title: Show HN: A data viewer for choosing Frigate-compatible IP cameras
content: The thread is a "Show HN" post introducing a data viewer for Frigate-compatible IP cameras. While a few users expressed positive interest in the project, the thread is largely dominated by concerns regarding potential spam, as one commenter pointed out that the OP and several other commenters appear to be bot accounts created just seven days ago. Additionally, a significant number of the comments in the thread were flagged as [dead].
